name: HDC2080 temperature & humidity sensor
description: Texas Instruments low-power digital temperature (-40 to 125 °C, ±0.2 °C typical) and relative humidity (0–100 %, ±2 %) sensor with 14-bit results over I2C at address 0x40 (0x41 with ADDR high). Runs on 1.62–3.6 V only. Sold as: TinkeringTech HDC2080 TI Humidity & Temperature Sensor Breakout (5-pin: 3.3V, INT, SCL, SDA, GND; 10 kΩ pull-ups to 3.3V on board, ADDR tied to GND, no regulator), I2C address 0x40.
eli5: Tells your board how warm the air is and how damp it is, using very little power.

pins.name: 3.3V
pins.description: Supply, 1.62–3.6 V straight to the chip (no regulator: never 5 V)

pins.description: DRDY/INT output, push-pull; high-impedance until enabled in register 0x0E (optional)

supplierQuery: HDC2080 humidity temperature sensor breakout I2C
buildNotes: Power it from 3.3 V only: the chip's maximum supply is 3.6 V and the board has no regulator.
Start a measurement by writing 0x01 to register 0x0F (14-bit T and RH, MEAS_TRIG); wait at least 1.3 ms (10 ms is safe), then read 4 bytes from 0x00: T low, T high, RH low, RH high (LSB first).
T = raw / 65536 × 165 − 40.5 °C; RH = raw / 65536 × 100 %. The two lowest bits of each word are always 0.
Manufacturer ID (0xFC/0xFD, LSB first) reads 0x5449 and device ID (0xFE/0xFF) 0x07D0: a quick way to confirm the wiring.
ADDR is tied to GND on this board, so the address is 0x40; it clashes with HDC1080, HTU21D/Si7021 and INA219 at their default addresses.
INT is optional and stays high-impedance unless DRDY/INT_EN (register 0x0E bit 2) is set.
Keep the sensor away from the ESP32 and regulators, which warm the air around them.

driver.code:
# HDC2080 temperature & humidity sensor (Texas Instruments), MicroPython driver.
# Written from the TI datasheet (SNAS678C): on-demand mode (AMM = 000), 14-bit T and RH.
# Registers are 8 bits wide with auto-increment; results are 16-bit words sent LSB first
# (0x00 = T low, 0x01 = T high, 0x02 = RH low, 0x03 = RH high), the 2 lowest bits always 0.
import time

_ADDR = 0x40          # ADDR pin to GND or open; 0x41 with ADDR to VDD
_REG_TEMP_L = 0x00
_REG_INT_CONF = 0x0E  # SOFT_RES, AMM[2:0], HEAT_EN, DRDY/INT_EN, INT_POL, INT_MODE
_REG_MEAS_CONF = 0x0F # TRES[1:0], HRES[1:0], RES, MEAS_CONF[1:0], MEAS_TRIG
_REG_MANUF_ID_L = 0xFC
_MANUF_ID = 0x5449
_DEVICE_ID = 0x07D0
_MEAS_START = 0x01    # TRES = 14 bit, HRES = 14 bit, MEAS_CONF = humidity + temperature, MEAS_TRIG = 1


class HDC2080:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=_ADDR, vdd=None):
        """vdd: optional supply voltage, to apply the datasheet's PSRR correction (Equation 2)."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.vdd = vdd
        time.sleep_ms(3)  # the sensor needs at most 3 ms after power-up
        ids = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _REG_MANUF_ID_L, 4)
        manuf = ids[0] | (ids[1] << 8)
        dev = ids[2] | (ids[3] << 8)
        if manuf != _MANUF_ID or dev != _DEVICE_ID:
            raise OSError('HDC2080 not found at 0x%02x (IDs %04x/%04x): check the wiring' % (addr, manuf, dev))
        # Auto measurement off, heater off, DRDY/INT pin high-Z: measurements start over I2C.
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _REG_INT_CONF, bytes([0x00]))

    def read(self):
        """Measure once and return (temperature in °C, relative humidity in %)."""
        self.i2c.writeto_mem(self.addr, _REG_MEAS_CONF, bytes([_MEAS_START]))
        # Conversion: 610 µs (T, 14 bit) + 660 µs (RH, 14 bit) typical; wait well past it.
        time.sleep_ms(10)
        d = self.i2c.readfrom_mem(self.addr, _REG_TEMP_L, 4)  # LSB first, as the datasheet requires
        t_raw = d[0] | (d[1] << 8)
        h_raw = d[2] | (d[3] << 8)
        # Datasheet Equation 1: T = raw / 2^16 * 165 - 40.5 °C; Equation 3: RH = raw / 2^16 * 100 %
        t = t_raw * 165 / 65536 - 40.5
        if self.vdd is not None:
            t += 0.08 * (self.vdd - 1.8)  # Equation 2: TEMP_PSRR = 0.08 °C/V for supplies above 1.8 V
        return t, h_raw * 100 / 65536

    def temperature(self):
        return self.read()[0]

    def humidity(self):
        return self.read()[1]

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from hdc2080 import HDC2080

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = HDC2080(i2c)
while True:
    t, h = sensor.read()
    print('T=%.1fC H=%.1f%%' % (t, h))
    time.sleep(1)
